records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts: The read of booking.attendees (lines 26-42) and the attendee write (lines 92-106) are not in a transaction, so two concurrent addGuests requests can both pass the uniqueness filter and create duplicate Attendee rows (TOCTOU race).

addGuests.handler.ts: The attendee dedup uses an exact case-sensitive comparison (guest === attendee.email), so a case-variant of an existing attendee's stored email defeats the dedup and writes a second persistent record for the same person that no later exact-match code path will recognize as the same human.
records.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, deduplication filters out existing attendees via an exact string match: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`. Inputs (`guests`) are validated as emails but not normalized (e.g., lowercased), while the blacklist is lowercased, so a case-variant like `User@Example.com` vs `user@example.com` can bypass dedup and create a duplicate attendee record

records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts (lines 153-160): The EventManager used to update the organizer's calendar event is constructed with the caller's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) instead of the organizer's — the organizer's credentials are fetched but never used.
records.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the `EventManager` used for `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` is instantiated with `credentials` from `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and spread `...user` (the caller), not the booking organizer.
